homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field, and the Labor addendum names no homonym in this row's T. No card is a homonym: all eight cards concern bossware. Card 1 is the entity; card 2 is another study of the class (a distinct entity, below); cards 3–8 concern the term. 'Bossware' is the class the database's name carries, not a sense of the name; 'Coworker Worktech Database' (T1-7) is a variant the composition took from the URL slug (CAP-1-12), not a homonym; 'Little Tech' is the report's name for the marketplace the database catalogues and the census lists 'Little Tech database' as an alias.

captures.description: THE BOSSWARE AND EMPLOYMENT TECH DATABASE, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'The Coworker.org Bossware and Employment Tech Database catalogs more than 550 labor-focused technology products used to monitor, track, and manage workers across various industries.' A definition of bossware (from the New York Times card), four kinds of feature, thirteen named products in three groups, and Vanderbilt Law School's research on data sharing. Eight cards: Coworker's own page, Vanderbilt, the New York Times and five videos or posts.
